findings.severity: high (silent lost write on the most common edit)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-layout/src/textflow.rs:38-49 (map_pos: pos >= end goes after the insertion), :81-118 (replace_story_text re-splits the touched region so the paragraph still starts at P), :208-238 (shift_paragraph_records maps the record to P+n, then first_per_start drops it because P+n is no paragraph start); callers harness-view layout_ui.rs:1133-1134, layout_ui/find.rs:97-98
findings.what: Take a pure insertion (start == end == P) at the first byte of paragraph k > 0. The paragraph keeps starting at P in the edited story: the previous paragraph is touched because its end equals P, and the re-split cuts at its terminator. But map_pos moves every key at P to P+n. shift_paragraph_records then finds no paragraph at P+n and drops both the paragraph_composition entry and the paragraph_flows entry of that paragraph. The lane's tests insert at byte 1, inside paragraph 0 (indent_spacing.rs:568, viewer_layout_styles.rs ReplaceText start 1), so this path is never covered. At byte 0 (ruling 4) the outcome differs: replace_story_text maps paragraph 0 to start n, so bytes [0, n) belong to no paragraph, and the record survives at n.
findings.scenario: Story "aa\nbb", paragraphs [0,3) and [3,5), with a paragraph_composition entry {left_indent 30 pt} and a split-column paragraph_flows entry, both at 3. Run LayoutEdit::ReplaceText{start:3,end:3,text:"x"}. The edited paragraphs are [0,3) and [3,6), both entries map to 4, and both are dropped. The second paragraph loses its indent and its split columns, with no error. The same holds for any paste at a paragraph start and for find/change with an empty hit at a paragraph start.
findings.fix: Write the red tests first (ruling 4): insertion at byte 0, at P > 0 with "x", and at P > 0 with "x\n". Then map paragraph-keyed records to the start of the edited paragraph that contains the mapped position of the old paragraph's first byte (snap to the containing paragraph). With that rule "x" at P keeps the key at P, "x\n" at P moves it to P+2, and merges and whole-paragraph deletes keep today's first-touched result. In replace_story_text, start the first touched region at min(p.start, start) so an insertion at byte 0 is covered by paragraph 0. Use the same rule in both functions so paragraph starts and keys cannot diverge.

findings.severity: medium (wrong answer: missing paragraph space in balanced columns)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-layout/src/threaded_reflow.rs:1116-1119 (gap_at set to the column where the gap was added), :1560-1563 (Meta.gap = gap only if the first line landed in that same pos/col), :822-866 (balance_band re-adds m.gap only at rows > 0)
findings.what: Take a paragraph whose gap pushed its first line into the next column, or whose first line opened a column. It records Meta.gap = 0. Balancing then moves lines between columns (k = ceil(L/n) per column), so that first line can end up mid-column with no space above it. The rule is "no space at a column top", but after balancing the line is no longer at a column top.
findings.scenario: Two columns, 3 lines deep, vertical_balance_columns on. Paragraph A has 3 lines and fills column 0. Paragraph B has 1 line and space_before 6 pt, so it lands at the top of column 1 and the gap is dropped (Meta.gap 0). Balancing gives column 0 = A1, A2 and column 1 = A3, B. B sits at row 1 with extra 0, so its baseline is 12 pt below A3 instead of 18 pt. balancing_keeps_paragraph_space (indent_spacing.rs:446) only covers gaps that were already mid-column.
findings.fix: Store the paragraph's resolved gap on its first line's Meta whatever column it landed in (k == 0 gives gap), and drop the gap_at match. balance_band already drops the gap at row 0 and keeps its `return false` when the result no longer fits. Add a red test with the case above.

findings.severity: medium (wrong answer on both Adobe composers)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-layout/src/threaded_reflow.rs:1300-1311 (re-break when natural_width > narrowed), :1317-1325 (last_overfull = natural_width > w), :1462 and :1471 (overfull turns off alignment, justification and compress_line), :1520-1521 with adobe_composer.rs:353-364 (Adobe composers set a line wider than its slot by compressing its spaces)
findings.what: The last-line fit test uses the natural width only. The Adobe single-line and paragraph composers may choose a last line that is tighter than its slot, and the set stage then closes it with compress_line. With a positive last_line_indent, a last line the composer would compress into the narrowed width triggers a needless re-break. If the re-broken last line is still a little over by natural width, it is flagged overfull, and overfull suppresses the compression that would have made it fit. The line then overhangs the indent and reports Line.overfull = true. The test at indent_spacing.rs:345 accepts `width <= 24 || overfull`, so it cannot catch this.
findings.scenario: AdobeSingleLine or AdobeParagraph, Left aligned, last_line_indent set so the narrowed last line is 1-2 % narrower than its natural width while its spaces can absorb the difference. Expected: the line is compressed and fits. At a300982c: it is re-broken or marked overfull, and it is set uncompressed past the indent.
findings.fix: For the Adobe composers, judge fit the way the set stage does: natural width minus the compressible space, from the paragraph's word_spacing minimum through compress_line's model, must not exceed w. Alternatively take the fit from the breaker's own overfull flag on a break run at the narrowed width. Add one test per Adobe composer with a compressible last line.

findings.certainty: READ (code and log); the cost under the gate is UNVERIFIED
findings.severity: medium (refusal point and hang risk; the stop rule is still open)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-layout/src/threaded_reflow.rs:1300-1311; adobe_composer.rs:779-783 (flat_from is the first index after which the width stays constant); log Handshake_Artifacts/WP-KERNEL-STUDIO/smb-type-indent-spacing-1/smb-type-indent-spacing-1-measure-last-line-b8d51d15.log
findings.what: Ruling 1 (re-break only when the narrowed width holds the widest word) is not in a300982c. The measurement also does not show what the re-break costs once that gate passes. In the 30 pt case the re-break never fired on FirstFit, AdobeSingleLine or AdobeParagraph: line counts stayed at 120, 360 and 1000, and FirstFit would gain one line if it re-broke. It fired only on Knuth-Plass (96 to 97 lines). So the lane note "a normal 30 pt indent costs at most one extra pass ... others unchanged" does not cover AdobeParagraph. Narrowing index l moves AdobeParagraph's flat_from to l+1, which makes every line index up to l a distinct state. The 5000-word budget_exceeded at 170 pt may come from that state count and not only from infeasibility. Split paragraphs get no re-break at all (breaks are taken at :1271), so their narrowed last line goes straight to overfull. The declared reading and the DESCRIPTOR say "one bounded re-break (positive, Latin)" without stating this exception.
findings.scenario: A 5000-word paragraph, AdobeParagraph, 180 pt measure, last_line_indent 100 pt (the narrowed 80 pt holds every word of the toy font). The re-break passes the gate, flat_from moves to about line 1000, and the cost or refusal is unmeasured. With the gate added, this is the case that decides the brief's stop rule.
findings.fix: Implement the gate on the boxes of the first result's last line: the widest unbreakable box run between glue, hyphen included when the break is flagged. Re-run the measurement with an indent that passes the gate and forces the re-break, on all four composers, in debug and release, at 600, 1800 and 5000 words. If the AdobeParagraph or Knuth-Plass refusal point still moves, stop and send the numbers (brief item 3). State the Split exception in notes.declared_readings and in the DESCRIPTOR, or apply the same re-break there.

findings.severity: medium (silent lost write through the drive row)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/layout_ui/styles.rs:164-176 (the patch replaces the style's whole style_composition record); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/action/commands/layout.rs:30 (patch text: "composition: Folio StudioCompositionSettings (indents and spacing in pt)")
findings.what: The drive text reads as an indent setter. The command replaces the whole record. A model or caller that sends {"composition":{"left_indent":...}} to a style that already holds composer, H&J or hyphenation settings (an IDML-imported style always does) erases all of them with no notice. The replace behaviour appears only in the lane's notes.declared_readings, which no caller reads.
findings.scenario: A paragraph style imported from IDML carries composition_scope every_line, hyphenation true and word spacing 80/100/133. layout.style.edit_style with patch {composition:{left_indent:{value:12,unit:"pt"}}} indents the paragraph, but it also switches back to the request composer, turns hyphenation off and resets the spacing.
findings.fix: Either overlay the patch on the stored record (existing.overlaid(&patch); an explicit null still clears the whole record) and say so in the patch text, or keep replace and write "replaces the style's whole composition settings record" into the patch text at layout.rs:30 and the StylePatch doc. Add one test that pins whichever behaviour is chosen, starting from a record with hyphenation set.
